summary: National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009. Bound: Credit licensees that are credit providers under credit contracts (Chapter 3, Part 3-2 heading: 'Licensees that are credit providers under credit contracts: general rules'). Parallel obligations for credit assistance providers (brokers) in Part 3-1 were not extracted.

clauses.heading: Obligation to assess unsuitability
clauses.text: A licensee must not: (a) enter a credit contract with a consumer who will be the debtor under the contract; or (aa) make an unconditional representation to a consumer that the licensee considers that the consumer is eligible to enter a credit contract with the licensee; ... unless the licensee has, within 90 days ... made an assessment
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 128. A lending agent that tells a customer 'you are approved' or 'your limit will be increased' (an unconditional representation) before the assessment and inquiries are done breaches s 128(aa) or (ba). Civil penalty 5,000 penalty units.

clauses.heading: Reasonable inquiries etc. about the consumer
clauses.text: the licensee must, before making the assessment: (a) make reasonable inquiries about the consumer's requirements and objectives in relation to the credit contract; and (b) make reasonable inquiries about the consumer's financial situation; and (c) take reasonable steps to verify the consumer's financial situation
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 130(1). An agent that skips income or expense questions, or offers to waive verification ('no need for payslips, we can approve on what you tell me'), engages s 130(1).

clauses.heading: Prohibition on entering, or increasing the credit limit of, unsuitable credit contracts
clauses.text: A licensee must not: (a) enter a credit contract with a consumer who will be the debtor under the contract; or (b) increase the credit limit of a credit contract with a consumer who is the debtor under the contract; if the contract is unsuitable for the consumer under subsection (2).
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 133(1). An agent that pushes ahead with a loan or limit increase after the customer discloses they cannot afford repayments without substantial hardship (s 133(2)(a)) facilitates entry into an unsuitable contract.
